PROJECT 01
E-commerce SQL Analytics Platform

End-to-end analytics platform on a synthetic e-commerce dataset. Covers cohort retention, funnel analysis, RFM segmentation, rolling revenue, market basket, and geo roll-up — the six analytical patterns used daily in product and commercial data roles.

PostgreSQL 15 Python Matplotlib Pandas 500 users · 8k orders · 40k events
📊
01 / 06
Cohort Retention
Which signup cohorts retain best over 6 months?

Monthly cohort matrix tracking what % of users placed at least one order in each of the 6 months following signup. Key technique: GENERATE_SERIES to force zero-retention months to appear explicitly — a common data quality trap.

Nov 2023 cohort hits 77.8% Day-0 retention — holiday shoppers who converted immediately
Non-linear patterns suggest opportunistic buyers driven by promotions, not habits
No cohort consistently outperforms → channel segmentation needed for a real signal
CTEs Window functions GENERATE_SERIES
🔽
02 / 06
Conversion Funnel
Where do users drop off between browsing and buying?

Session-level funnel from view → cart → checkout → purchase per category, using COUNT DISTINCT FILTER — cleaner than multiple subqueries.

High view-to-cart + low cart-to-purchase gap signals price anxiety
Actionable: test price-match CTA or instalment payment at checkout
COUNT DISTINCT FILTER Session aggregation
👥
03 / 06
RFM Segmentation
Which customers are Champions, At Risk, or Lost?

Scored every customer on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary value using NTILE(5) window functions, then mapped combined scores to CRM segments. Output feeds directly into campaign targeting.

Champions → loyalty rewards
At-Risk VIPs → win-back offers
Lost → suppress or reactivation sequence
NTILE(5) Window functions CRM segments
📈
04 / 06
Rolling Revenue
What is the true revenue trend, free of weekly noise?

7-day and 30-day rolling GMV using ROWS BETWEEN window frames, plus month-over-month growth via LAG.

7-day line → live dashboard view, smooths day-of-week noise
30-day line → leadership reporting layer
MoM column separates real growth from seasonal spikes
ROWS BETWEEN LAG Rolling GMV
🛍️
05 / 06
Market Basket Analysis
Which products are most frequently bought together?

Self-join on order_items with product_a_id < product_b_id to generate pair combinations without duplicates. Computes support, confidence, and lift — the foundation of Apriori association rule mining.

Output feeds directly into a cross-sell recommendation engine
High-lift pairs identify non-obvious product affinities
Self-join dedup Support / Lift Association rules
🌍
06 / 06
Geographic Revenue Roll-up
Which markets drive the most GMV and at what AOV?

GROUP BY ROLLUP produces country subtotals and a grand total in a single query pass — equivalent to three UNION ALL queries but far more efficient. GROUPING() flags subtotal rows for downstream consumption in Python or a BI tool.

Country-level GMV, AOV, and order count in one pass
GROUPING() makes it safe to consume in Pandas or Tableau
GROUP BY ROLLUP GROUPING() AOV
PROJECT 02
Collaborative Filtering Recommender System

Production-style recommender system on MovieLens 100K. Modular codebase separating data, model, and evaluation concerns. Treats ratings as implicit feedback — mirroring real-world systems where you have clicks or purchases, not star ratings. Achieves HR@10 of 0.384 on a held-out test set.

ALS Matrix Factorization implicit numpy · scipy MLflow 943 users · 1,682 movies · 100k ratings

🧠 Problem framing

Codebase is split into three independent modules — data_loader, model, and evaluation — mirroring how production ML systems separate concerns. Ratings are treated as implicit feedback: any interaction signals interest regardless of score, which is the standard assumption when you have clicks or purchases rather than explicit ratings.

⚙️ Algorithm: ALS

Decomposes R ≈ U × Vᵀ into latent factor matrices, alternating between fixing U and solving for V (each step has a closed-form solution). Confidence weighting: c_ui = 1 + α × r_ui + L2 regularisation.

PROJECT 03
Signal — Systematic Stock Screener

An interactive web app that screens the S&P 500 on momentum and quality factors, builds a portfolio, and backtests it against the market. Built as a personal research tool — a repeatable framework, not a price predictor.

Python Streamlit yfinance pandas Plotly ~500 stocks · live data

📊 What it does

Pulls live price and fundamental data for the full S&P 500, scores every stock on a composite factor model, selects the top N, and runs a buy-and-hold backtest against SPY — all in an interactive dashboard with adjustable signals and weighting.
